findings.method: Exact analytic counterexample to an intermediate lemma plus emptiness proof for the stated gap hypothesis; no numerical experiment.
findings.parameters: a=2^(-1/2), b=2^(-7/6)*(3*pi)^(2/3), delta=1/8, integer n≥max(2,N0(delta)), T=delta^(-1)*n^(1/3); admissible ensemble L=S.
findings.assumptions: S is unit-variance Brownian Gibbs by source Lemma2.5, and S1(t)+a*t^2 has a fixed finite marginal by Lemma2.6; a quantile supplies the uniform pointwise K(epsilon). Thus Assumption2.8 is nonempty. Twice differentiability, not C2, is sufficient.
findings.complete_check: If |h''+a|≤delta and |h+a*t^2+b*n^(2/3)|≤delta*n^(2/3)/2, then g=h+a*t^2+b*n^(2/3) has g''≥a-delta. Convexity gives g(T)+g(-T)-2g(0)≥(a-delta)T^2, while the value bound gives at most2*delta*n^(2/3). This requires a≤delta+2delta^3=33/256, false. The event asserted to have probability≥7/8 is empty. Separately, at j=n,t=0, x_n≥f_n implies the printed |x_j-b*(n^(2/3)-j^2)-f_n|≥b*(n^2-n^(2/3)), exceeding delta_n*n^(2/3) for sufficientlylarge n. Fn(0) is empty although3.17 asserts probability>3/4.
findings.alternative_readings: Original source images and separate240dpi image confirm exponents. Ordinary derivatives and local differentiation17.36 exclude an unconventional derivative normalization. Boundary labels reversed inDefinition2.2 are read in the consistent intended order fromDefinition2.1.
findings.core_dependency: Theorem3.16 -> Lemma3.23 -> Lemma3.21 -> verification ofAssumption3.18 -> Theorem3.19; togetherwithProposition3.20 -> Theorem2.9.
findings.impact_limit: Major because the presented core intermediate claim and its use are false. Not a counterexample to the main characterization, nor a counterexample to Theorem3.19 with satisfiable assumptions. Related normalization slips counted once.
findings.repair_status: Replacing second-derivative +2^(-1/2) with +sqrt2 and j^2 with j^(2/3) removes the demonstrated contradictions. Exact quadratic h0 verifies local consistency, not random-curve approximation. Section17's actual local proof supports corrected curvature. Reciprocal factors in3.19–3.20 must match sqrt2 Airy gaps. A full coordinated corrected proof was not certified.

checks.source_locations: arXiv2308.11908v2 PDF pp.29-30 and38; Lemmas2.5-2.6 and3.21(3)
checks.reason: The actual source images show h''+2^(-1/2) together with approximation by -2^(-1/2)t^2-b n^(2/3). For delta=1/8,T=delta^-1 n^(1/3), g=h+a t^2+b n^(2/3) satisfies g''>=a-delta. Convexity gives second difference >=(a-delta)T^2, while the uniform value bound gives <=2delta n^(2/3), forcing a<=33/256, contrary to a=1/sqrt2>1/2. Twice differentiability suffices for this convexity argument. Source Lemma2.5 and stationary marginal Lemma2.6 provide the admissible L=S example and a finite-quantile K(epsilon), so the probabilistic hypotheses are nonempty.

The actual detail image confirms j^2. At j=n,t=0, the ordered bridge lies above f_n, so the absolute deviation is at least b(n^2-n^(2/3)), exceeding delta_n n^(2/3) for large n. The stipulated high-probability event is empty. This invalidates the printed verification of the hypothesis, rather than furnishing a counterexample to Theorem3.19 under satisfiable assumptions.

Lemma3.21 is explicitly used to verify Assumption3.18, then Theorem3.19 and Proposition3.20 yield Theorem2.9. That is a core derivation failure under the stated severity contract. The actual local Section17 calculations instead use +sqrt2 curvature, and the Airy gap normalization is sqrt2(S_j-S_(j+1))=A_j-A_(j+1). Correcting curvature, j^(2/3), and all reciprocal gap displays consistently removes these algebraic contradictions. The quadratic h0 only proves local consistency, not approximation of the random curve or the full corrected proof.

Direct substitution of q=2^(-1/6) into S^(q)(t)=q^-1 S(q^2t) gives 2^(-1/3)A(2^(-1/3)t)-t^2/2. At zero its CDF is F_TW(2^(1/3)z), matching(25.1), whereas the corollary's additional2^(-1/2) gives F_TW(2^(5/6)z). A finite nonzero nondegenerate random variable cannot be invariant in law under a strict positive contraction. The proof itself concludes S^(q). Removing the extra factor repairs this secondary application; centering signs must be consistent but are immaterial to the time-zero contradiction. Main characterization does not depend on it, supporting Minor.
